title: St. Barts: villas, beaches and island time
seoTitle: St. Barts: villas, beaches and island time | EXJET
description: Plan a St. Barts holiday around villa life, beach days and Gustavia, with practical arrival and household coordination notes for private travel teams.

facts.label: The focus
facts.value: Villa stays and time on the water

sections.heading: Choose the rhythm of the island
paragraphs: St. Barts combines villa stays with beach days and time in Gustavia. Saline, Saint-Jean and Shell Beach offer different settings; choose the daily atmosphere before choosing an address. A family gathering may call for a quieter villa routine, while a couples’ trip can leave more room for restaurants and evenings in town.

sections.heading: Build the stay around one base
paragraphs: Use the villa as the centre of the itinerary. Reserve a few defining lunches or a day on the water, then keep the remaining days open. Confirm bedroom distribution, steps, pool arrangements, staff accommodation and the actual services included. For a holiday with several households, one shared preference brief prevents competing instructions reaching the property team.

sections.heading: Coordinate the final connection
paragraphs: Review the complete journey to the island with the flight advisor and local transfer provider before fixing an arrival dinner. Confirm the final air or sea connection, baggage acceptance and what happens if the inbound journey changes. The principal’s flight, luggage movement and villa handover should form one workable schedule, including an alternative arrival plan.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Name the villa contact and agree the handover window.
Share baggage dimensions, children’s equipment and separate household arrivals.
Confirm restaurant and boat bookings directly, including their cancellation terms.

title: Turks and Caicos: a considered beach escape
seoTitle: Turks and Caicos: a considered beach escape | EXJET
description: Explore Turks and Caicos for a family beach holiday, from Grace Bay to a villa stay, with clear planning notes for accommodation, transfers and boat days.

facts.label: The focus
facts.value: Beach time and family villa stays

sections.heading: Start with the setting
paragraphs: Grace Bay on Providenciales combines a long beach with resort accommodation, restaurants and shops. It is a useful starting point for families who want a beach holiday without a full programme of excursions. Decide whether the priority is walkable dining, a staffed villa or a resort with activities before comparing individual properties.

sections.heading: Leave room for the water
paragraphs: Plan one boat day early in the stay and retain another possible date. A fixed lunch and a rigid excursion schedule can make a beach holiday feel rushed. Ask the boat provider about shade, boarding arrangements, children’s equipment and the route appropriate to the day’s conditions. Water activities should reflect each guest’s confidence and ability.

sections.heading: Make the arrival specific
paragraphs: Provide the exact property address when discussing the flight and transfer. A stay elsewhere in the island group needs a separate connection plan; a booking described simply as Turks and Caicos is not detailed enough. Match vehicle capacity to the whole party and its baggage, then agree who receives any revised arrival time.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Confirm room proximity and any steps between bedrooms and the beach.
List dietary preferences and children’s needs before the stay.
Keep one flexible day for weather-sensitive activities.

title: The Bahamas: Exuma and Harbour Island
seoTitle: The Bahamas: Exuma and Harbour Island | EXJET
description: Compare Exuma and Harbour Island for a Bahamas holiday. Plan the island, accommodation and final boat or air connection around the way your party travels.

facts.label: Suggested pace
facts.value: One island base, with optional day trips

sections.heading: Choose the island before the aircraft
paragraphs: The Bahamas is an island itinerary, not a single resort destination. Exuma’s cays and coastal scenery lend themselves to time on the water. Harbour Island offers a smaller village setting, while neighbouring Eleuthera provides a different scale of exploration. Decide how much moving around the party wants before arranging accommodation.

sections.heading: Keep the itinerary geographically coherent
paragraphs: A villa stay with a few local outings can be more comfortable than trying to collect several islands in a short trip. If a yacht or second island is part of the plan, treat the move as a travel day. Ask the marine provider to choose activities around conditions and responsible wildlife practices, rather than building the day around a promised encounter.

sections.heading: Resolve the last leg
paragraphs: Share the exact island, property and dock where relevant. The flight advisor and accommodation team need to agree the arrival point, onward connection and baggage movement. Confirm who handles a delayed arrival and whether an overnight alternative is needed. For separate households, a common arrival brief is particularly useful when the last leg is by boat.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Record the island and property name on every booking.
Check boat boarding, luggage storage and transfer operating arrangements.
Agree a weather alternative with the accommodation and transport providers.

title: Los Cabos: coast, cuisine and time together
seoTitle: Los Cabos: coast, cuisine and time together | EXJET
description: Plan a Los Cabos escape with a clear choice of neighbourhood, villa or resort, plus thoughtful dining, boating and aircraft charter arrival coordination.

sections.heading: Distinguish the two towns
paragraphs: Los Cabos includes Cabo San Lucas and San José del Cabo, linked by a resort corridor. San José offers an art-focused town setting; Cabo San Lucas has its own marina-centred rhythm. Choose the accommodation address around the activities that matter, rather than treating the region as one compact resort.

sections.heading: Balance the resort and the region
paragraphs: A strong short stay needs only a few anchors: a considered dinner, a day on the water or a round of golf. Leave the rest for the property and the coast. Ask the hotel or villa team which beaches suit the planned activity and current conditions; a sea view does not establish swimming suitability. Confirm restaurant and course access directly.

sections.heading: Compare the complete arrival
paragraphs: Los Cabos has more than one airport option. Share the actual property location and proposed aircraft so the advisor can compare the flight with the ground transfer. The operating carrier must confirm the airport and itinerary. For a celebration, separate the arrival day from the main hosted event so a schedule change does not disrupt the whole gathering.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: State whether the stay is in San José, Cabo San Lucas or the corridor.
Confirm golf reservations, equipment transport and dining preferences.
Agree the resort handover and transfer contact before departure.

title: Palm Beach: a coastal stay with cultural depth
seoTitle: Palm Beach: a coastal stay with cultural depth | EXJET
description: Shape a Palm Beach stay around the coast, Worth Avenue, cultural visits and family time, with practical notes for residence and aircraft arrival planning.

facts.label: Suggested pace
facts.value: A long weekend or a longer residence stay

sections.heading: Look beyond the beach
paragraphs: Palm Beach combines an Atlantic setting with historic architecture, Worth Avenue and cultural institutions. The Flagler Museum and the Society of the Four Arts offer options for days away from the water. The right itinerary balances these visits with time at the residence or hotel, instead of treating every day as an excursion.

sections.heading: Plan around the household
paragraphs: A short hotel stay and a month at a family residence have different needs. For the latter, coordinate the property team, vehicles, visiting guests and the principal’s work commitments before adding restaurants. Keep one calendar for family activities and fixed appointments, with clear distinctions between confirmed plans and suggestions.

sections.heading: Connect the arrival to the address
paragraphs: Share the actual residence or hotel address, baggage and passenger requirements with EXJET when comparing flights. Ask the ground provider to account for the day’s local conditions. For guests arriving separately, agree a reception plan so the host or household team is not managing several last-minute handovers while preparing for the stay.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Confirm residence readiness and the named arrival contact.
Book cultural visits against current opening and ticket arrangements.
Keep guest transport and the principal’s schedule in the same brief.

title: The Hamptons: a summer residence itinerary
seoTitle: The Hamptons: a summer residence itinerary | EXJET
description: Plan a Hamptons stay around the right village, household routine and coastal activities, with a clear flight and ground transport brief for the travel team.

facts.label: Suggested pace
facts.value: A long weekend or an extended stay

sections.heading: Choose the address first
paragraphs: The Hamptons combines Atlantic beaches with village life on Long Island’s East End. The exact residence matters more than the broad destination name: it determines the everyday journey to friends, restaurants and activities. Start with where the family wants to spend its time, then assess the transport around that location.

sections.heading: Keep a residence stay easy
paragraphs: Anchor the weekend with one or two gatherings and protect unplanned time at the house. Agree guest numbers, household staffing, parking and any property restrictions before accepting invitations or arranging a hosted dinner. If a wine-country visit is important, plan it as a separate outing rather than squeezing it between beach time and an evening commitment.

sections.heading: Treat transport as a live plan
paragraphs: Have the flight advisor compare suitable arrival options and the current operating arrangements for the proposed date. Do not assume a local airport or a past itinerary is available for a new flight. Confirm the destination address with the driver and allow a flexible transfer window. Separate luggage movement can be worth discussing for a longer residence stay.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Share the village, exact address and property access instructions privately.
Check current beach access arrangements with the accommodation team.
Keep the departure day clear of tightly timed social commitments.

title: Napa Valley: wine, dining and a slower pace
seoTitle: Napa Valley: wine, dining and a slower pace | EXJET
description: Plan a Napa Valley escape with thoughtful winery appointments, dining and transfers. A practical guide for private clients, hosts and executive assistants.

sections.heading: Choose a base around the appointments
paragraphs: Napa Valley includes distinct towns such as Napa, Yountville, St. Helena and Calistoga. Select the base after identifying the wineries and restaurants that genuinely interest the party. A shorter daily route leaves more time to enjoy the visits and avoids turning a relaxed trip into a succession of transfers.

sections.heading: Make fewer, better appointments
paragraphs: Start with two substantial experiences in a day and protect time for lunch. Ask each estate what the visit includes, whether it is private, and how long to allow. A familiar label does not guarantee access to a particular cellar or host. For collectors, share interests in advance; for mixed groups, include appealing options for guests who do not drink.

sections.heading: Separate the flight from the tasting day
paragraphs: Keep the arrival day light and arrange a dedicated driver for winery visits. Share the hotel address, appointment locations and expected luggage with the aviation advisor. If bottles will be purchased, discuss shipping with the estate and review applicable arrangements separately from passenger baggage. Do not build the departure around a final appointment with no margin.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Confirm dietary requirements and non-drinking guests’ preferences.
Record each appointment’s host, duration, deposit and cancellation terms.
Arrange driving and any wine shipping before the first visit.

paragraphs: Aspen has a distinct winter and summer rhythm. Winter brings skiing and snow activities; summer combines outdoor recreation with an arts and cultural programme. Choose the season around the family’s priorities, then select a base that supports both active guests and those who prefer a slower day in town.

sections.heading: Organise the mornings, protect the afternoons
paragraphs: For a ski stay, align instruction, equipment fitting and meeting points before arrival. Group guests by ability and ambition rather than age alone. For summer, alternate an outdoor day with a cultural visit or a quiet afternoon. Confirm the current programme directly with venues instead of assuming an event repeats on the same dates each year.

sections.heading: Keep the mountain arrival flexible
paragraphs: Share ski equipment, winter clothing and the complete passenger list when reviewing aircraft options. The operating carrier needs to assess the actual flight and airport conditions; a previous arrival is not a guarantee for the next trip. Agree an alternative arrival and ground-transfer plan, and avoid placing a non-refundable activity immediately after touchdown.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Confirm the accommodation’s access to the intended daily activities.
List equipment dimensions and arrange rentals where useful.
Assign one contact to update the driver, property and instructors.

title: Vail: a mountain holiday for the whole party
seoTitle: Vail: a mountain holiday for the whole party | EXJET
description: Explore Vail for ski holidays and summer mountain stays. Coordinate the village, activities, equipment and arrival around every member of the party.

sections.heading: Choose the village deliberately
paragraphs: Vail Village and Lionshead each provide a base for a mountain stay. Lionshead’s gondola links the village to skiing in winter and mountain activities in summer. Choose the exact accommodation by the daily meeting point and the needs of non-skiers, rather than by a broad promise of proximity to the slopes.

sections.heading: Give different guests different days
paragraphs: A multigenerational trip works best when everyone can choose a pace. Schedule instruction and equipment for skiers, then offer a separate village, gallery or wellness plan for others. Summer can combine walking and outdoor time with visits such as the Betty Ford Alpine Gardens. Keep shared lunches or dinners as the natural meeting points.

sections.heading: Coordinate equipment and arrival together
paragraphs: Ask the flight advisor to review aircraft baggage capacity against the full equipment list. Arrange a vehicle that accommodates both people and luggage, and review a weather alternative with the operating carrier and transfer provider. A comfortably planned arrival day is more useful than an optimistic promise to reach a lesson immediately after the flight.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Specify Vail Village, Lionshead or the exact residence location.
Confirm lesson meeting points and equipment fitting arrangements.
Keep a separate activity option for guests taking a day off the mountain.

title: Saint-Tropez: the Riviera at your own pace
seoTitle: Saint-Tropez: the Riviera at your own pace | EXJET
description: Plan Saint-Tropez around a villa, beach days, dining and time on the water. Coordinate the Riviera stay and final transfer with a clear travel brief.

facts.label: The focus
facts.value: Riviera villa life and coastal dining

sections.heading: Choose between the village and the retreat
paragraphs: Saint-Tropez combines Provençal character with a Mediterranean resort setting. Beach time, dining, shopping and cultural visits can all feature, but the choice of base shapes the stay. Decide whether the party wants to be close to the village or spend more time at a villa with its own household routine.

sections.heading: Give the itinerary breathing room
paragraphs: Arrange a small number of priority reservations and leave space between them. A beach lunch, a boat outing and an evening in town need not all fall on the same day. For a villa gathering, confirm staffing, catering permissions and guest numbers with the property team before planning hosted events. Check the current opening calendar with individual venues.

sections.heading: Plan the final journey in detail
paragraphs: The accommodation address and any yacht embarkation point should guide the arrival discussion. Ask EXJET to compare suitable aircraft and airport options with the onward transfer, then have the relevant operators confirm each leg. A helicopter or marine connection requires its own availability, baggage and weather review; it should never be assumed from the flight booking.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Confirm the exact villa address and vehicle access.
Record the marina and yacht contact if the itinerary continues by sea.
Keep transfer time separate from the first restaurant reservation.

title: Monaco: culture, the coast and event-led travel
seoTitle: Monaco: culture, the coast and event-led travel | EXJET
description: Plan a Monaco stay around culture, dining or a confirmed event, with practical notes on accommodation, access, ground transfers and an onward Riviera itinerary.

sections.heading: Let the purpose set the calendar
paragraphs: Monaco offers a concentrated cultural setting, from opera and music to exhibitions and performance. A quiet cultural break and an event-led visit call for different planning. Choose the reason for the trip first, then confirm the actual performance or event dates before committing the travel around them.

sections.heading: Make access explicit
paragraphs: A hotel booking, event ticket and hospitality package are separate commitments. Record exactly what each reservation includes, which guests are named and whether access can be transferred. For a cultural stay, choose a few performances or visits and leave time for dining and the coast. A compact destination can still benefit from an unhurried programme.

sections.heading: Connect Monaco with the wider Riviera
paragraphs: Give the advisor the hotel, any marina meeting point and the fixed arrival requirement. Compare the international flight and final ground or other transfer as a complete journey. If a yacht is involved, have its captain confirm the embarkation plan directly. Maintain an alternative transfer rather than making the itinerary depend on a single connection.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Verify event dates and named ticket holders with the organiser.
Distinguish confirmed hospitality from a requested reservation.
Share the accommodation and embarkation details with each transport provider.

title: Lake Como: villas, gardens and days on the water
seoTitle: Lake Como: villas, gardens and days on the water | EXJET
description: Plan a Lake Como holiday with a thoughtful lakeside base, garden visits and boat days, plus practical notes for property access and airport transfers.

sections.heading: Choose the shore around the stay
paragraphs: Lake Como’s villages, gardens and historic villas make the lake itself part of the itinerary. Bellagio, Varenna and the western shore each create a different daily pattern. Choose the base around the visits and dining that matter, rather than assuming every lakeside address provides an equally convenient starting point.

sections.heading: Combine the water with one clear purpose
paragraphs: A boat outing can connect a garden visit, lunch and time on the lake. Confirm which sites require timed admission and whether the proposed boat can use the relevant landing point. Villa del Balbianello and Villa Carlotta are examples of places to research with the local guide. Keep an alternative on land for a day when boating is unsuitable.

sections.heading: Make the handover practical
paragraphs: A lakeside property may have separate road and water access arrangements. Ask the accommodation team to identify the correct arrival point for passengers and baggage. Share it with the flight advisor and driver, together with any stairs or mobility requirements. The final transfer should be planned to the property entrance, not merely to the nearest town.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Confirm the room or villa layout, steps and arrival entrance.
Book gardens and boat services against their current operating arrangements.
Agree who receives luggage if passengers arrive by water.

title: The Amalfi Coast: a stay shaped around the sea
seoTitle: The Amalfi Coast: a stay shaped around the sea | EXJET
description: Explore the Amalfi Coast through a well-chosen base, coastal visits and boat days. Plan the property access and transfers before committing a busy itinerary.

sections.heading: Select one base with care
paragraphs: The Amalfi Coast combines steep coastal landscapes, small bays, cultivated terraces and distinctive towns. A view is only one part of choosing a property. Consider steps, road access and the effort involved in reaching restaurants or the water, particularly for a family party with different mobility needs.

sections.heading: Trade a checklist for a few good days
paragraphs: Choose one or two places to explore in depth, with a boat day where appropriate. Amalfi, Positano and the wider coast deserve time rather than a sequence of brief stops. Confirm the guide’s meeting point and realistic route before making a lunch reservation elsewhere. For a celebration, keep the main occasion at or close to the accommodation.

sections.heading: Resolve land and water transfers
paragraphs: The aircraft arrival is one part of the journey. Ask the local provider to compare the road transfer and any boat connection for the actual date, party and baggage. Identify a workable road alternative if water travel changes. Property staff should confirm the final entrance and baggage handover, especially when the accommodation is reached through pedestrian lanes or steps.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Ask specifically about steps, lifts and vehicle access.
Confirm the vessel, landing point and weather alternative for boat days.
Leave a clear margin between checkout, transfer and the flight.

title: Tuscany: a country house, wine and cultural days
seoTitle: Tuscany: a country house, wine and cultural days | EXJET
description: Plan a Tuscany villa stay around Chianti or Val d’Orcia, with wine appointments, cultural visits and practical household and transport coordination.

sections.heading: Choose a region within the region
paragraphs: Tuscany rewards a focused itinerary. Chianti and Val d’Orcia offer different landscapes and village routes; Val d’Orcia combines rolling agricultural scenery with towns such as Pienza and Montalcino. Choose the area around the interests of the party, then select the house and transport. A broad regional address can disguise a demanding daily drive.

sections.heading: Let the house carry part of the holiday
paragraphs: Alternate an excursion with a day at the property. A wine appointment, a village walk or a cultural visit can each be the main event rather than components of one crowded day. Confirm cooking arrangements, household staffing and dietary preferences directly with the property team. For collectors, request a specific wine experience instead of assuming a general tasting includes cellar access.

sections.heading: Brief the arrival beyond the town name
paragraphs: Provide the exact estate address and vehicle access instructions when planning the flight and ground journey. Ask whether the approach suits the proposed vehicle and how luggage will be handled. If guests arrive from several cities, consolidate the handover information in one brief while keeping individual passenger details restricted to the providers who need them.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Confirm the location of bedrooms, pool arrangements and staff accommodation.
Group visits by area to reduce time spent in vehicles.
Record winery appointments and any private-use terms in writing.

title: Sardinia: Costa Smeralda and a coastal itinerary
seoTitle: Sardinia: Costa Smeralda and a coastal itinerary | EXJET
description: Plan a Sardinia stay around Costa Smeralda, Porto Cervo and time on the water, with clear villa, yacht and flight-arrival coordination for the travel team.

sections.heading: Give the coast a clear starting point
paragraphs: Costa Smeralda combines coastal scenery with resort life, while Porto Cervo provides a focal point for marinas, dining and shopping. Decide whether the stay is primarily on land or aboard a yacht. That choice should guide the accommodation, arrival timing and how much travelling is built into each day.

sections.heading: Design around the party’s interests
paragraphs: For a land-based stay, choose a small number of beach or boat outings and protect time at the villa or hotel. For a yacht itinerary, let the captain shape the route around conditions and the confirmed arrangements. A suggested anchorage or restaurant is not a reservation. Guests who prefer to remain ashore should have an equally considered plan.

sections.heading: Join the flight to the embarkation
paragraphs: Send the exact property or marina details to the aviation advisor, and ask the yacht team to confirm the boarding location. Review baggage with both providers; what fits on a business jet may not fit comfortably into the onward vehicle or tender. Preserve time for the handover rather than planning an immediate departure from the marina.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Confirm the property or yacht contact who will receive the party.
Separate marina arrangements from restaurant and beach reservations.
Review luggage and the weather alternative for the final connection.

title: Ibiza: villas, coastal days and the old town
seoTitle: Ibiza: villas, coastal days and the old town | EXJET
description: Plan an Ibiza holiday around the right villa setting, coastal activities and Dalt Vila, with practical notes for mixed-age groups and transport coordination.

facts.label: The focus
facts.value: Villa stays, coastal outings and island culture

sections.heading: Choose the atmosphere before the address
paragraphs: Ibiza can support very different trips. A quiet villa stay, a social holiday and a family gathering need different surroundings and daily routines. Include a visit to Dalt Vila, whose fortified walls and historic lanes offer a cultural counterpoint to the coast. Let the party’s preferences determine the base rather than its reputation alone.

sections.heading: Make room for different interests
paragraphs: Agree which evenings and outings the group wants to share, then allow independent plans. Confirm venue opening dates, age policies and reservations directly. A private house should also be checked for guest limits, noise rules and permission for any hosted event. For a boat day, ask the provider for an itinerary suited to the party and conditions.

sections.heading: Keep arrivals coordinated
paragraphs: Provide the full villa address, access instructions and each household’s arrival window. The flight and vehicle plan should account for staff, children’s equipment and luggage as well as the principal. If the itinerary includes onward travel by sea, identify the boarding point and the provider responsible for the handover before confirming a tightly timed connection.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Confirm the property’s event, guest and household-service arrangements.
Reserve cultural visits and dining around the actual travel dates.
Keep a quiet-day option for guests with different interests.

title: Mykonos: the island and a day on Delos
seoTitle: Mykonos: the island and a day on Delos | EXJET
description: Plan a Mykonos stay with a clear villa brief, time on the coast and a considered visit to Delos, plus practical notes for transfers and group preferences.

sections.heading: Balance the social stay with the setting
paragraphs: Mykonos provides a base for a coastal holiday, while nearby Delos adds a substantial historical dimension. Delos is an archaeological destination with its own visitor arrangements, not simply another beach stop. Decide whether the trip centres on a villa, social evenings or cultural exploration before selecting the accommodation.

sections.heading: Give Delos its own day
paragraphs: Ask a qualified local guide to shape the visit around the party’s interests, walking ability and current access arrangements. Confirm the sea connection, meeting point and what to bring. Keep another possible date if the transport changes. The rest of the stay can remain simple: time at the property, a few chosen meals and a boat outing where suitable.

sections.heading: Coordinate the land and sea handovers
paragraphs: Share the exact villa location and road access with the ground provider. Review the complete passenger and baggage list when requesting a flight, particularly if different households are joining. Any onward island or yacht connection needs separate confirmation. An itinerary should name who updates the villa, driver and marine provider if the arrival time moves.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Confirm the villa’s steps, room layout and vehicle access.
Check Delos admission and boat arrangements with the current providers.
Agree which activities are shared and which are optional for the group.

seoTitle: St. Moritz: the Engadine in winter and summer | EXJET

paragraphs: St. Moritz combines an alpine setting with art, shopping and cultural life. Corviglia, the Upper Engadine lakes and the Segantini Museum give the destination more than one character. A winter sports trip and a summer lakeside stay deserve different programmes; agree the focus before selecting accommodation and travel dates.

sections.heading: Build a balanced mountain stay
paragraphs: For winter, coordinate instruction and equipment early, with a separate plan for guests who do not ski. In summer, combine outdoor time with a cultural visit and leave a day without a fixed schedule. Ask activity providers about the requirements of the proposed excursion rather than assuming every scenic experience suits every member of the party.

sections.heading: Give the flight plan flexibility
paragraphs: The operating carrier must assess the proposed mountain arrival, aircraft and current conditions. Ask the aviation advisor to compare suitable options with the final ground journey, and agree an alternative before departure. Share equipment dimensions and confirm that the onward vehicle can carry them. Keep the arrival day free of a costly, tightly timed appointment.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Match the accommodation to the daily activity meeting points.
Confirm equipment fitting and the plan for non-skiers.
Name one coordinator for changes affecting the property and transfer.

title: Gstaad: chalet life and a quieter mountain pace
seoTitle: Gstaad: chalet life and a quieter mountain pace | EXJET
description: Plan a Gstaad chalet holiday around village life, mountain activities and household preferences, with a clear brief for accommodation and arrival coordination.

facts.label: Suggested pace
facts.value: A week with room to settle in

sections.heading: Start with the village rhythm
paragraphs: Gstaad combines chalet architecture with a car-free promenade, shops and access to the surrounding valleys and mountains. It suits a holiday where the accommodation and daily routine matter as much as a list of activities. Choose the base according to how easily the party wants to reach the village and the proposed outings.

sections.heading: Make the chalet brief precise
paragraphs: Bedroom numbers alone do not describe a family stay. Confirm which rooms connect, where staff will stay, what household services are included and how meals will be arranged. In winter, align ski instruction and equipment with each guest’s ability. At other times, ask local providers for walks and excursions that suit the whole party rather than choosing solely by the view.

sections.heading: Compare arrivals as complete journeys
paragraphs: Provide the chalet address and baggage list to the flight advisor. The aircraft operator should confirm the suitability of the proposed airport and flight, with a workable onward transfer and alternative. Agree how the property team receives updates. A household-ready chalet and a clear arrival handover often contribute more than an extra activity on the first day.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Request a room plan and a written list of included household services.
Identify the daily meeting point for lessons or guided outings.
Confirm vehicle capacity for guests, staff and seasonal equipment.

title: Courchevel: choose the village, then the chalet
seoTitle: Courchevel: choose the village, then the chalet | EXJET
description: Plan a Courchevel ski or summer stay with a clear village choice, chalet requirements and practical notes for equipment, lessons and mountain transfers.

facts.label: The focus
facts.value: Ski holidays and alpine summer stays

sections.heading: Be specific about the village
paragraphs: Courchevel includes several villages, including Courchevel 1850, Moriond, Village, Le Praz, La Tania and Saint-Bon. They do not create identical daily routines. Choose the accommodation around the intended meeting point, access and atmosphere, especially when the group includes children or guests who prefer time away from the slopes.

sections.heading: Plan the first full day before arrival
paragraphs: Confirm equipment fitting, instruction and the meeting location, then leave the arrival evening uncomplicated. For a chalet stay, agree meals, household staffing and room distribution in advance. Summer offers a different programme of mountain time and village activities; confirm the current operating calendar with each provider rather than transferring a winter plan to another season.

sections.heading: Review the mountain transfer honestly
paragraphs: A destination name does not establish that a particular aircraft can land nearby. Have the operating carrier assess the actual flight and discuss the final journey with the ground provider. Any helicopter connection requires its own confirmation and alternative. Build the schedule around a reliable complete journey, with room for the conditions of the day.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Record the village and exact chalet entrance on the itinerary.
Check the current resort calendar for the travel dates.
Agree a transfer alternative and equipment handling before departure.

title: Paris: art, dining and time to explore
seoTitle: Paris: art, dining and time to explore | EXJET
description: Plan a Paris cultural escape around art, dining and neighbourhood time, with practical notes for private visits, reservations and executive-assistant coordination.

paragraphs: Zermatt’s official arrival guide describes a car-free destination, with private cars left in Täsch and the journey continued by train or an authorised transfer. Do not brief an ordinary airport car as a direct hotel drop-off. Have the accommodation confirm the final approach and local reception, including how luggage and ski equipment reach the property.

sections.heading: Choose the stay around the mountain day
paragraphs: For skiers, compare access to the intended lifts, equipment storage and meeting points for instruction. For a mixed party, consider the village routine for guests who are not skiing. A chalet or hotel should make both days straightforward, with a clear way for the group to meet for lunch or at the end of the afternoon.

sections.heading: There is a winter day beyond skiing
paragraphs: Zermatt publishes marked winter walks and snowshoe itineraries. Choose a route with local advice about current conditions, effort and suitable equipment. In a warmer season, review hiking options afresh rather than assuming the winter plan translates directly. Mountain weather and lift operations can change the day, so retain an alternative close to the accommodation.

sections.heading: Give the transfer chain room
paragraphs: Plan the air arrival, onward road or rail journey and final village transfer as one sequence. Confirm which provider receives the party at each change, especially when travelling with children or several sets of equipment. Avoid placing the first fixed mountain activity immediately after the scheduled arrival. The group’s first afternoon can simply be time to settle in.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Confirm the car-free arrival sequence with the property.
List ski equipment and luggage for every transfer stage.
Balance mountain activities with a clear plan for non-skiers.

faqs.question: Can a standard airport car drive straight to a Zermatt hotel?
faqs.answer: Zermatt is car-free. Confirm the permitted onward arrangement from Täsch and the final local transfer with the accommodation, including luggage and equipment handling.

title: Mauritius: a coastal stay with an island beyond it
seoTitle: Mauritius Travel Guide: Coastal Stays, Nature & Seasons | EXJET
description: Plan a Mauritius holiday around the coast, the season and time inland. Compare beach days, western landscapes and a practical arrival brief for the family.

facts.label: The focus
facts.value: Coastal stays, nature and island discovery

sections.heading: Choose a coast and a daily routine
paragraphs: Begin with the balance of beach time and exploration. A property that suits a week largely on site may be a different choice from one intended as a base for inland outings. Ask about the exact beach setting, room layout and activities available during the proposed dates. For several generations, confirm what each guest can enjoy without a substantial daily transfer.

sections.heading: Give the west a day of its own
paragraphs: Mauritius’ official tourism guide brings together the landscapes of Black River Gorges, Le Morne and Chamarel in its western region. Select a focused outing rather than trying to cover them all at once. A viewpoint visit and a guided hike require different time, footwear and ability. Have a local specialist match the route to the people travelling.

sections.heading: Read the season at island level
paragraphs: The official climate guide describes November to April as summer and May to October as winter, with wetter summer conditions. This is a seasonal framework, not a forecast for a particular resort. Ask the accommodation and activity providers about the chosen coast, current conditions and alternatives to water-dependent outings. Avoid treating all Indian Ocean destinations as interchangeable.

sections.heading: Make the arrival brief useful to the household
paragraphs: Share the exact accommodation, room-readiness arrangements and ground reception contact with the travel team. For a longer stay, record sporting equipment and any separate arrivals before reviewing aircraft options. Keep the first day light and make clear which bookings are confirmed by the property, which by an excursion provider and which by the aviation team.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Select the coast before comparing room and residence options.
Check the seasonal fit of the planned outdoor activities.
Assign a receiving contact to each separate family arrival.

sources.label: Mauritius Tourism Promotion Authority — the west

faqs.question: Is the same season suitable for every Indian Ocean island?
faqs.answer: Each destination has its own climate and operating calendar. For Mauritius, review the chosen coast, the time of year and the planned activities with the relevant local providers.

title: Niseko: a Hokkaido mountain stay for the whole party
seoTitle: Niseko Travel Guide: Ski Stays, Summer Trails & Planning | EXJET
description: Compare Niseko bases for skiing, dining and summer mountain time, with practical guidance on equipment, transfers and arrangements for non-skiing guests.

facts.label: The focus
facts.value: Snow sports, mountain scenery and Japanese dining

sections.heading: Choose the base before the residence
paragraphs: Japan’s tourism organisation describes Niseko as a group of connected ski areas, with different places to stay around the mountain. Hirafu has a concentration of accommodation and dining. Compare the actual location, lift access and evening routine rather than treating every Niseko address as equivalent. A quieter residence may require more planned transport.

sections.heading: Match the mountain day to the guests
paragraphs: Confirm instruction, equipment rental and meeting points for each skier or snowboarder. Mixed abilities can mean different daily schedules, so decide where the party will reunite. For non-skiers, establish an enjoyable plan around the accommodation, dining and locally confirmed activities. Proximity to a lift does not by itself resolve the needs of the whole family.

sections.heading: Consider Niseko outside the snow season
paragraphs: JNTO also highlights summer and autumn hiking in the Niseko area. A warm-season visit should have its own brief, based on the trails, weather and services operating at that time. Ask a local guide about route conditions and the demands of the proposed walk. Do not assume that the winter resort programme or its full restaurant offering continues unchanged.

sections.heading: Plan the Hokkaido ground journey carefully
paragraphs: When reviewing flights, include the onward journey to the chosen property and the time needed for luggage and equipment. Ask the ground provider to confirm vehicle capacity and arrangements appropriate to the conditions. Keep the arrival day free of tightly timed lessons or dining commitments. For an EA, the essential handover is from the aircraft itinerary to the team receiving the guests at the residence.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Specify the village or ski-area base and the exact property.
Record each guest’s instruction, rental and non-skiing plans.
Allow the arrival schedule to accommodate the onward road journey.

faqs.question: What should a family office compare when choosing a Niseko base?
faqs.answer: Compare the exact residence location, lift access, evening transport and arrangements for non-skiers. Confirm instruction and equipment plans separately for each participant.

title: Villa and private-island holidays: the planning brief
seoTitle: Villa and private-island holidays: the planning brief | EXJET
description: Plan a villa or private-island holiday with a clear brief for room layouts, household services, guest arrivals and the final flight, road or boat connection.

sections.heading: Define the stay before choosing the property
paragraphs: Start with the number of households, the preferred level of seclusion and the kind of daily service required. A villa, an island resort and an exclusive-use property are different propositions. St. Barts, Tuscany and the Maldives illustrate different settings, but the deciding details are the actual layout, location and confirmed inclusions of the property under review.

sections.heading: Turn preferences into a usable room plan
paragraphs: Ask for a floor plan, bedroom locations and information about stairs, pools and access to the water. Identify connecting rooms, accommodation for staff and space for guests who need to work. Confirm whether cooking, housekeeping, laundry and vehicles are included or separately arranged. A photograph or a bedroom count cannot answer these practical questions.

sections.heading: Agree the service and guest arrangements
paragraphs: Give the household or property team one consolidated brief covering dietary needs, meal routines and visiting guests. Confirm event permissions, external suppliers and cancellation terms before arranging a celebration. Distribute personal preferences only to the people responsible for delivering them. Keep requests distinct from services that have been accepted and priced in writing.

sections.heading: Coordinate the complete arrival
paragraphs: Work backwards from the property handover. Confirm the final air, road or boat connection, its baggage capacity and its operating arrangements. Then ask EXJET to align suitable flight options with that plan. Separate household arrivals need an agreed reception contact and an alternative if one leg changes; a private address does not remove the need for careful coordination.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Property: layout, access, privacy expectations and included services.
People: household arrivals, staff, dietary needs and named decision-maker.
Journey: final connection, luggage handover and change contact.

title: Yacht and jet itineraries: connect the two journeys
seoTitle: Yacht and jet itineraries: connect the two journeys | EXJET
description: Coordinate a private flight with a yacht itinerary through clear embarkation details, baggage planning, transfer ownership and practical contingency arrangements.

facts.label: Suggested pace
facts.value: A flexible connection at each end

sections.heading: Begin with the confirmed embarkation
paragraphs: The flight should be planned around the yacht’s actual embarkation point and agreed boarding time. A broad destination such as Sardinia, the Bahamas or the Riviera is not enough. Obtain the marina or meeting location from the yacht team and confirm whether guests board alongside or transfer by tender. The captain determines the marine operating plan.

sections.heading: Keep the responsibilities clear
paragraphs: The aircraft, yacht and local transfer may involve separate providers and agreements. Name one coordinator to reconcile their schedules without assuming that one booking covers another. Confirm who meets the party, who handles luggage and who communicates a changed arrival. A yacht itinerary can evolve with conditions; the flight team needs the latest confirmed plan, not an early proposal.

sections.heading: Match baggage to the smallest leg
paragraphs: A large aircraft cabin does not guarantee that the onward vehicle, tender or yacht storage suits every bag. Share dimensions and equipment requirements with each provider. Soft luggage may be requested by the yacht team; verify the actual instructions before packing. Discuss separate luggage movement where appropriate, and keep essential personal items with the passenger.

sections.heading: Preserve a workable alternative
paragraphs: Avoid making an expensive charter connection depend on immediate boarding after touchdown. Agree a comfortable transfer window, a place to wait and an overnight option where relevant. Confirm how a change affects each separate agreement. EXJET can help coordinate the aviation brief; marine availability, routes and activity arrangements must be confirmed by the yacht provider.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Embarkation: exact location, boarding method and captain’s contact.
Transfers: named provider, passenger count and luggage capacity.
Changes: decision contact, alternative plan and separate contract terms.

title: Ski and chalet holidays: plan beyond the slopes
seoTitle: Ski and chalet holidays: plan beyond the slopes | EXJET
description: Plan a private ski holiday with the right chalet, instruction and equipment arrangements, plus a flexible flight and mountain-transfer brief for the whole party.

facts.label: Suggested pace
facts.value: A week with a flexible arrival day

sections.heading: Plan for the whole party
paragraphs: The best base is the one that supports the daily routine of this group. Record skiing ability, lesson preferences and the interests of non-skiers before choosing the property. Aspen, Vail, Courchevel, Gstaad and St. Moritz offer different village and cultural settings. Compare the exact accommodation with the proposed meeting points rather than relying on a general resort description.

sections.heading: Make the first morning straightforward
paragraphs: Confirm equipment fitting, instruction, lift arrangements and the meeting location in advance. Ask whether equipment can be prepared before arrival and who will help children reach their lessons. A chalet brief should include meals, staff accommodation, steps and room distribution. Keep a separate plan for guests who prefer a cultural visit, a village day or time at the property.

sections.heading: Review equipment before choosing the aircraft
paragraphs: Provide the quantity and dimensions of skis, boards, boots and ordinary baggage when requesting a flight. The proposed aircraft and onward vehicle both need to accommodate the real load. Ask the operating carrier to review the actual itinerary and conditions. Neither a model’s published performance nor a previous trip establishes that a new mountain flight is suitable.

sections.heading: Keep the arrival flexible
paragraphs: Agree an alternative airport or transfer plan with the relevant providers before departure. A helicopter connection needs its own review and a workable backup. Avoid putting the first lesson or a non-refundable hosted dinner immediately after the planned arrival. For a family office, one current contact sheet should connect the aviation advisor, driver, property and ski team.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Guests: ability, instruction, mobility needs and non-skiing preferences.
Equipment: dimensions, rental decisions and vehicle capacity.
Arrival: operator-approved plan, alternative and property handover.

title: Safari and conservation travel: a considered approach
seoTitle: Safari and conservation travel: a considered approach | EXJET
description: Plan a safari around guiding, camp location and a manageable pace. Review family requirements, conservation claims and every transfer before confirming the journey.

facts.label: Suggested pace
facts.value: Fewer camp changes and more time in place

sections.heading: Choose the experience before the camp name
paragraphs: Discuss the party’s interests with a safari specialist: wildlife observation, photography, walking or learning about conservation. In the Okavango Delta, wetland and dryland environments create different settings. Ask why each proposed camp belongs in the itinerary and what activities are actually included. A longer stay in a well-chosen place can be more rewarding than frequent transfers.

sections.heading: Ask specific questions about guiding and access
paragraphs: Confirm guide arrangements, vehicle use, children’s policies and the requirements of each activity. Wildlife movements and natural conditions cannot be guaranteed. If a conservation visit is proposed, ask who operates it, what the visit involves and how any contribution is used. Avoid treating close animal contact or a private reserve label as evidence of responsible practice.

sections.heading: Make the remote-travel brief complete
paragraphs: Camp connections can have different luggage and scheduling requirements from the international flight. Confirm bag type, allowance and the handling of photographic equipment with each carrier. Ask the specialist to identify current entry and health guidance and the practical arrangements for support during the stay. Any individual medical questions belong with an appropriate clinician.

sections.heading: Coordinate the international and local plans
paragraphs: Have the safari provider and aviation advisor reconcile the whole journey, including what happens if the inbound flight moves. Keep the first camp day free of an activity that requires an exact arrival. If combining a safari with Cape Town or an island stay, check the baggage and transfer requirements again rather than assuming they remain the same throughout.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Camp brief: locations, guiding, private-use requests and inclusions.
Guest brief: interests, ages, mobility and equipment needs.
Journey brief: connection ownership, baggage and current specialist guidance.

title: Wine and gastronomy journeys: fewer, better appointments
seoTitle: Wine and gastronomy journeys: fewer, better appointments | EXJET
description: Plan a wine and dining holiday around real interests, confirmed access and a comfortable daily pace, with practical guidance for hosts, EAs and family offices.

facts.label: The focus
facts.value: Wine visits, dining and hosted experiences

facts.label: Suggested pace
facts.value: Two meaningful appointments in a day

sections.heading: Start with taste, not status
paragraphs: Ask what the party enjoys: a particular wine region, a producer, cooking, regional food or a restaurant. Napa Valley, Tuscany and Central Otago provide different contexts for a wine journey. A sought-after name is useful only if the actual experience suits the guests. Include an equally appealing plan for non-drinkers and people with dietary restrictions.

sections.heading: Clarify what an appointment includes
paragraphs: Confirm the host, format, duration, group size and whether the visit is private. A tasting does not automatically include a cellar tour or time with a winemaker. Record any deposits and cancellation terms, and share interests early enough for the provider to respond. For a dining-led trip, make the confirmed restaurant reservations the anchors of the schedule.

sections.heading: Leave space between experiences
paragraphs: Plan around a small number of substantial visits, with lunch and travel time protected. Arrange a driver for wine days. Avoid a sequence that requires every appointment to finish exactly on time, and do not place an elaborate meal immediately after a long flight. The quality of the day depends as much on its pace as on the venues.

sections.heading: Handle purchases separately from the itinerary
paragraphs: If guests expect to buy wine, discuss shipping, delivery and the applicable requirements with the estate or specialist. Do not assume that purchases can simply join the passenger baggage or move across borders without further arrangements. The EA’s final brief should separate the travel plan, reservations and purchase follow-up so each has a clear owner.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Preferences: interests, dietary requirements and non-drinking guests.
Appointments: named host, inclusions, duration and confirmed access.
Logistics: driver, realistic spacing and separate purchase arrangements.

title: Art and cultural travel: make access meaningful
seoTitle: Art and cultural travel: make access meaningful | EXJET
description: Plan an art or cultural holiday with the right guide, confirmed admission and a coherent itinerary, including practical notes on private visits and event-led travel.

facts.label: Suggested pace
facts.value: One major cultural experience each day

sections.heading: Define the interests behind the trip
paragraphs: A cultural itinerary should reflect the party’s curiosity: a period of art, architecture, music, theatre or a place’s history. Paris, London and Kyoto each support very different journeys. Choose a few meaningful experiences and ask a knowledgeable guide to connect them, rather than building the programme from a generic list of landmarks.

sections.heading: Be precise about private access
paragraphs: A private guide, a private tour and exclusive access are not interchangeable. Ask the provider to describe the exact arrangement, the named venue, timing and permissions. Confirm admission separately where required. After-hours access, specialist meetings and invitations should remain requests until the responsible venue or host has accepted them in writing.

sections.heading: Respect the place and the people
paragraphs: Check photography, dress, conduct and accessibility requirements before the visit. In Kyoto, for example, visitors are asked not to stop or photograph geiko and maiko in the street without permission. A considerate itinerary works within the rules of the institution and the local community. It does not promise to bypass them.

sections.heading: Coordinate the day around its fixed points
paragraphs: Treat performances, timed admissions and hosted visits as the anchors, then fit meals and transfers around them. Leave room for conversation and unplanned discovery. For an event-led holiday, verify dates and ticket terms with the organiser before committing flights. Share a concise daily brief with the guests, while the assistant retains the full booking and contact record.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Purpose: interests, preferred depth and the right specialist guide.
Access: exact inclusions, venue permissions and ticket arrangements.
Pace: realistic transfers, accessibility and time to enjoy the visit.

title: Wellness retreats: space to rest, thoughtfully planned
seoTitle: Wellness retreats: space to rest, thoughtfully planned | EXJET

facts.label: The focus
facts.value: Rest, gentle activity and a lighter schedule

facts.label: Suggested pace
facts.value: A settled stay with few fixed commitments

sections.heading: Define what rest means for this guest
paragraphs: A quieter holiday can mean time by the sea, mountain walks, a spa setting or simply fewer commitments. Ask the principal what should feel different from daily life before selecting a property. An island resort and an alpine stay create different routines. A wellness label alone does not establish the quality or suitability of the experience.

sections.heading: Check the actual programme
paragraphs: Review which activities and facilities are included, which require reservations and whether participation is optional. Confirm the credentials and scope of any specialist service directly. This is leisure planning; it should not rely on promises of medical outcomes, detoxification or guaranteed results. Individual health needs and treatment decisions require appropriate professional advice.

sections.heading: Protect time without over-managing it
paragraphs: Keep a few preferred activities and allow the guest to choose the rest during the stay. Confirm dining flexibility, quiet-room preferences and the expected communication routine. For a family office or EA, agree which matters should reach the principal and which can be handled by the travel team. A lighter itinerary is a deliberate choice, not an incomplete one.

sections.heading: Make the journey support the stay
paragraphs: Compare the complete travel time, connections and arrival handover before choosing the destination. A remote property may be appealing, but the final transfer should suit the guest. Build a gentle first day after a long flight and avoid placing a rigid appointment immediately after arrival. Confirm any activity changes directly with the provider.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Preferences: quiet, activity level, dining and communication expectations.
Property: actual facilities, programme inclusions and reservation rules.
Journey: manageable connections and a light arrival day.

title: Multigenerational holidays: one plan, different priorities
seoTitle: Multigenerational holidays: one plan, different priorities | EXJET
description: Plan a family holiday across generations with clear room arrangements, flexible activities and coordinated arrivals, designed for executive assistants and family offices.

facts.label: Suggested pace
facts.value: One comfortable base with optional activities

sections.heading: Gather preferences before choosing the destination
paragraphs: Start with the needs of every household: ages, mobility, food preferences, activity interests and how much time guests want together. A beach holiday in Turks and Caicos, a mountain stay in Vail and a city visit to London solve different problems. Choose the setting that supports the group rather than asking everyone to fit one person’s ideal programme.

sections.heading: Make the accommodation do more of the work
paragraphs: Request a room plan and identify connecting rooms, quiet spaces, steps and accommodation for accompanying staff. Confirm pool and water access arrangements directly with the property. Shared meals and a comfortable common area can hold the holiday together without requiring the whole group to join every outing. Keep the property’s actual services separate from optional requests.

sections.heading: Create shared anchors and optional days
paragraphs: Choose a few occasions everyone wants to share, then offer different activities at different paces. Name the person responsible for each smaller group and confirm who handles changes. For children, agree the care arrangements with the family and provider; do not assume that a general hotel service covers a particular requirement. Leave downtime between the main occasions.

sections.heading: Give the EA one reliable source of truth
paragraphs: Maintain a current itinerary with household arrivals, room allocation, transfer contacts and confirmed bookings. Share only the details each provider needs. Provide the full baggage and equipment brief when selecting aircraft, and reconcile separate arrivals before the trip. EXJET’s role is to help plan the aviation journey around those requirements; accommodation and activities require their own confirmations.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: People: named coordinator, household preferences and decision authority.
Stay: room plan, staff arrangements and shared gathering spaces.

title: Golf holidays: secure the round, then shape the journey
seoTitle: Golf Holiday Planning for Private Clients & Family Offices | EXJET
description: Plan a golf holiday around confirmed course access, tee times, equipment and the wider party. A practical brief for executive assistants and family offices.

facts.label: The focus
facts.value: Course access, equipment and time together

facts.label: Suggested pace
facts.value: Build the stay around confirmed rounds

sections.heading: Start with access to the course
paragraphs: A destination name is not a tee-time confirmation. Identify the course, the number of players and the dates, then ask about its current booking process, eligibility and any accommodation requirement. Keep requested, provisional and confirmed rounds clearly separated in the itinerary. Flights and hotel choices should reflect the access actually secured.

sections.heading: Compare two very different booking models
paragraphs: Pebble Beach publishes tee-time arrangements tied to resort reservations and date-specific conditions. At St Andrews, the Old Course has its own allocation routes, including a ballot. A ballot entry is not a reserved round. These examples show why an EA needs the course’s current written terms rather than a general assurance of access from a destination guide.

sections.heading: Make room for the rest of the party
paragraphs: Ask which guests intend to play every day and which prefer a mixed holiday. A second morning round may suit the golfers while a shared lunch, cultural visit or afternoon at the property suits everyone. Confirm transport for separate groups and agree where they will meet. Do not make non-playing companions dependent on the golfers’ finishing time.

sections.heading: Brief clubs as equipment, not ordinary luggage
paragraphs: Record the number and dimensions of golf bags alongside suitcases when requesting aircraft options. Confirm how the equipment will move through every ground transfer and whether rental sets are a better fit for part of the party. Schedule practice, caddies or buggies with the course where available, and retain a weather alternative for the day.

sections.heading: For the travel brief
bullets: Obtain the exact course, confirmed tee time and applicable terms.
Record player requirements and the plan for non-playing guests.

faqs.question: Should flights be booked before the preferred golf rounds are confirmed?
faqs.answer: Where a particular course is the reason for travelling, establish the access and booking conditions first. A request or ballot entry should not be presented as a confirmed tee time.

faqs.question: What belongs in the aircraft brief for a golf trip?
faqs.answer: Include the passenger count, suitcase details and the number and dimensions of golf bags. Ask the operator to confirm suitability for the actual aircraft and include the equipment in the ground-transfer brief.

facts.value: Choose the experience, then the window

sections.heading: Begin with the reason for travelling
paragraphs: Decide whether the holiday depends on skiing, a particular event, time on the water or simply a week together. That distinction determines which dates are flexible. For an EA or family office, record school calendars, household commitments and each traveller’s available window before circulating a destination shortlist. A compelling place is useful only when its operating season matches the proposed stay.

sections.heading: A planning calendar, not a weather promise
paragraphs: The examples below are starting points for a conversation. Seasons vary by hemisphere and locality: Queenstown’s winter falls in June to August, while Mauritius describes November to April as summer. Jackson Hole’s tourism guide identifies mid-June to mid-September as a peak visitor period. The actual opening calendar, weather and available services still need checking for the precise dates.

paragraphs: A pleasant forecast does not establish that the desired restaurant, lift, boat service or residence programme will operate. Obtain the provider’s calendar and booking conditions. For a shoulder-season holiday, choose a base that remains worthwhile if a particular outing is unavailable. For an event-led stay, use the organiser’s confirmed date rather than last year’s schedule.

faqs.question: What does shoulder season mean for a holiday brief?
faqs.answer: It describes a period outside a destination’s main peak, but it does not guarantee lower prices, good weather or full services. Confirm the accommodation, dining and activity calendar for the exact dates.

faqs.question: How should an EA narrow a seasonal destination shortlist?
